    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.RingTheory.Ideal.Operations, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Complements on ideal multiplication and the ideal action #

    This file collects general facts about the multiplication of ideals and about the action I • N of an ideal on a module, complementing Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Operations.lean.

    Main results #

    • Ideal.eq_one_of_mul_eq_one: a two-sided left factor of the unit ideal is the unit ideal. Over a commutative semiring, this implies that the divisor antidiagonal of the unit ideal is a singleton.
    • Ideal.toAddSubgroup_mul_eq_closure_mul: additive generators of a product of ideals.
    • Ideal.smul_top_eq_top_of_pi: an ideal that expands the whole of a product of modules expands the whole of every factor.
    • Ideal.smul_top_eq_comap_mul: the action on an ideal identifies its product submodule.
    • Ideal.span_range_fin_two_eq_top_iff: a pair generates the unit ideal exactly when its entries are coprime.
    • LinearMap.apply_mem_of_mem_smul_top: a linear functional carries I • M into I.
    • Ideal.span_insert_eq_top_of_subset: a generating set S may be replaced by a set S', both taken together with a common element a, as soon as every element of S is a itself or belongs to S'.
    • IsSMulRegular.of_span_singleton_le: if a regular element belongs to the principal ideal generated by another element, then the latter is regular.
    • Ideal.span_pair_sq_eq_span_singleton_of_isCoprime: if x ^ 2 = z m with z and m coprime, then (z, x) ^ 2 = (z).
    • IsSMulRegular.span_singleton_mul_right_mono and IsSMulRegular.span_singleton_mul_right_inj: multiplication by the principal ideal of a regular element preserves and reflects inclusion and equality of ideals.
    • Ideal.span_singleton_pow_sup_span_singleton_pow: the left ideals generated by a ^ j and a ^ m have as supremum the left ideal generated by a ^ min j m.
    • Ideal.sup_pow_le_sup_pow_right: modulo a two-sided ideal I, powers of I ⊔ J are controlled by the corresponding power of the left ideal J.
    • Ideal.span_pair_pow_eq_span_singleton: if z (1 - t) = x ^ n with t ∈ (x, z) and the left ideals (x, z) and (z) are two-sided, then (x, z) ^ n = (z).
    • Ideal.isTwoSided_span_of_subset_center: a left ideal spanned by central elements is two-sided.
    • Submodule.mem_span_algebraMap_smul_iff: over an algebra A, the action on a submodule N of the left ideal spanned by a scalar x produces exactly the multiples x • w with w ∈ N.
    • Subalgebra.toSubmodule_sup_pow_restrictScalars_eq_top: if a subalgebra and a principal left ideal additively span the ambient algebra, and the subalgebra contains a generator of the ideal, then the same holds with the ideal replaced by any power.
    source
    theorem Ideal.toAddSubgroup_mul_eq_closure_mul {R : Type u_1} [Ring R] {I J : Ideal R} {S T : Set R} (hI : Submodule.toAddSubgroup I = AddSubgroup.closure S) (hJ : Submodule.toAddSubgroup J = AddSubgroup.closure T) :
    Submodule.toAddSubgroup (I * J) = AddSubgroup.closure (S * T)

    If S and T additively generate the ideals I and J, then their pairwise products additively generate I * J.

    source
    theorem Ideal.eq_one_of_mul_eq_one {R : Type u_2} [Semiring R] {I J : Ideal R} [I.IsTwoSided] (h : I * J = 1) :
    I = 1

    If a two-sided ideal times a left ideal is the unit ideal, then the first ideal is the unit ideal.

    source
    theorem Ideal.smul_top_eq_comap_mul {R : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] (I J : Ideal R) :
    J • ⊤ = Submodule.comap (Submodule.subtype I) (I * J)

    The product I * J, viewed as a submodule of I, is the action of J on I.

    source
    theorem Ideal.span_range_fin_two_eq_top_iff {R : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] (v : Fin 2 → R) :
    span (Set.range v) = ⊤ ↔ IsCoprime (v 0) (v 1)

    The two entries of a pair generate the unit ideal exactly when they are coprime.

    source
    theorem Ideal.smul_top_eq_top_of_pi {R : Type u_2} [Semiring R] {ι : Type u_3} {M : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (M i)] (I : Ideal R) (h : I • ⊤ = ⊤) (i : ι) :
    I • ⊤ = ⊤

    Expanding a product expands every factor: if I • ⊤ = ⊤ in ∀ i, M i then I • ⊤ = ⊤ in each M i. Thus properness of I • ⊤ in one factor implies properness in the product.

    source
    theorem Submodule.mem_span_algebraMap_smul_iff {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [AddCommMonoid V] [Module R V] [Module A V] [IsScalarTower R A V] (N : Submodule A V) (x : R) {v : V} :
    v ∈ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R A) x} • N ↔ ∃ w ∈ N, x • w = v

    For an R-algebra A, possibly noncommutative, the action on a submodule N of the left ideal spanned by a scalar x : R consists of the multiples x • w with w ∈ N. This extends the membership criterion from Submodule.ideal_span_singleton_smul to noncommutative algebras.

    source
    theorem IsSMulRegular.of_span_singleton_le {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] {a b : R} (hb : IsSMulRegular R b) (h : Ideal.span {b} ≤ Ideal.span {a}) :
    IsSMulRegular R a

    If a regular element b belongs to the principal ideal generated by a, then a is regular. Equivalently, regularity descends along an inclusion (b) ⊆ (a) of principal left ideals.

    source
    theorem IsSMulRegular.span_singleton_mul_right_mono {R : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] {a : R} (ha : IsSMulRegular R a) {I J : Ideal R} :
    Ideal.span {a} * I ≤ Ideal.span {a} * J ↔ I ≤ J

    Multiplication by the principal ideal of a regular element preserves and reflects inclusion of ideals. This generalizes Ideal.span_singleton_mul_right_mono, which assumes a domain and a nonzero element.

    source
    theorem IsSMulRegular.span_singleton_mul_right_inj {R : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] {a : R} (ha : IsSMulRegular R a) {I J : Ideal R} :
    Ideal.span {a} * I = Ideal.span {a} * J ↔ I = J

    Multiplication by the principal ideal of a regular element is injective on ideals. This generalizes Ideal.span_singleton_mul_right_inj, which assumes a domain and a nonzero element.

    source
    theorem Ideal.span_insert_eq_top_of_subset {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] {a : R} {S S' : Set R} (hsub : S ⊆ insert a S') (hspan : span (insert a S) = ⊤) :
    span (insert a S') = ⊤

    Replacing one generating set by another: if every element of S is either a itself or an element of S', then S' together with a generates the unit ideal as soon as S together with a does. Note that S' need not be contained in S, and may be larger: the hypothesis constrains only where the elements of S are found. Both spans contain a, so only the rest of S has to be accounted for.

    source
    theorem Ideal.span_singleton_pow_sup_span_singleton_pow {R : Type u_1} [Semiring R] (a : R) (j m : ℕ) :
    span {a ^ j} ⊔ span {a ^ m} = span {a ^ min j m}

    The left ideals generated by two powers of the same element have as supremum the left ideal generated by the smaller power.

    source
    theorem Ideal.isTwoSided_span_of_subset_center {A : Type u_2} [Semiring A] {s : Set A} (hs : s ⊆ Set.center A) :
    (span s).IsTwoSided

    A left ideal spanned by central elements is two-sided.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.apply_mem_of_mem_smul_top {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] (f : M →ₗ[R] R) {I : Ideal R} [I.IsTwoSided] {x : M} (hx : x ∈ I • ⊤) :
    f x ∈ I

    A linear functional f : M → R carries I • M into the ideal I: the ideal action on R itself is multiplication, and f is linear over it.

    source
    @[instance 100]
    instance Ideal.isTwoSided_sup {R : Type u} [Semiring R] (I J : Ideal R) [I.IsTwoSided] [J.IsTwoSided] :
    (I ⊔ J).IsTwoSided

    A supremum of two two-sided ideals is two-sided.

    source
    theorem Ideal.sup_pow_le_sup_pow_right {R : Type u} [Semiring R] (I J : Ideal R) [I.IsTwoSided] (n : ℕ) :
    (I ⊔ J) ^ n ≤ I ⊔ J ^ n

    The n-th power of the supremum of a two-sided ideal and a left ideal is contained in the first ideal plus the n-th power of the second.

    source
    theorem Ideal.span_pair_pow_eq_span_singleton {R : Type u} [Ring R] {x z t : R} {n : ℕ} [(span {x, z}).IsTwoSided] [(span {z}).IsTwoSided] (hz : z * (1 - t) = x ^ n) (ht : t ∈ span {x, z}) :
    span {x, z} ^ n = span {z}

    A pair generating a power of one of its members. If the left ideals (x, z) and (z) are two-sided and z (1 - t) = x ^ n for some t in (x, z), then (x, z) ^ n = (z). The two-sidedness hypotheses hold automatically in a commutative ring. Modulo z, the ideal (x, z) becomes (x), whose n-th power vanishes; conversely z = x ^ n (1 + t + ⋯ + t ^ (n - 1)) + z t ^ n.

    source
    theorem Ideal.span_pair_sq_eq_span_singleton_of_isCoprime {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] {z x m : R} (hx : x ^ 2 = z * m) (hm : IsCoprime z m) :
    span {z, x} ^ 2 = span {z}

    A pair whose square is principal. In a commutative semiring, if x ^ 2 = z m with z and m coprime, then (z, x) ^ 2 = (z). For a squarefree integer d = p m with p prime, applied to a square root x of d, this is the ramified factorization (p) = (p, √d) ^ 2.

    source
    theorem Subalgebra.toSubmodule_sup_pow_restrictScalars_eq_top {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [Semiring S] [Algebra R S] {T : Subalgebra R S} {I : Ideal S} {π : S} (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = I) (hπT : π ∈ T) (h : toSubmodule T ⊔ Submodule.restrictScalars R I = ⊤) (n : ℕ) :
    toSubmodule T ⊔ Submodule.restrictScalars R (I ^ n) = ⊤

    If every element of S is a sum of an element of a subalgebra T and an element of a principal left ideal I, and T contains a generator of I, then the same holds with I replaced by any power.
